headline: WEIGHT SURGERY: the verdict is in — the edit did not fix it
lede: The fair-horizon rescore of MIT's weight-space programming claim is now the headline of the lab page: six scored rows, one backend, one seed — and a plain negative, stated plainly. The first-pass cap-1024 verdict that misled everyone (including us) is retired, and every number's uncertainty sits on the table with it.

notes.text: #1506 closed shipped: /demos/weightsurgery.html now leads with the verdict table — base 4.0%/11.0% vs presence-penalty 3.0%/5.0% vs k256-edit 8.0%/11.0% (MATH/GSM8K, n=100 each) — with loop flags on GSM8K up 5%→20% for the edit. One squash merge, harness-proven (ws2check 40 gates + 39 mutants).

Found and disclosed while finishing: 8 rows on every MATH run were llama-cli startup banners captured instead of answers (same problem ids — worker restarts mid-run). Logged, excluded from drill-downs, quantified in the footnote: ≤0.7pp accuracy, −8pp finished on MATH only; GSM8K clean; no comparison flips.

The phrase 'MIT's edit never opened' turned out never to have existed on the page or any lab branch — audited anyway, then replaced with the affirmative: our all-layer scan independently ranked layer 19, one of MIT's two layers, second of 24 without their prior. A negative with the right address is still a real negative.

Ops gotcha recorded for the lanes: the rescue proxy caches jalfern.com HTML and ignores cache-buster query strings — curl polls reported a shipped page as stale for 20 minutes. Verify prod through a second egress or by hashed asset.
